item.title: Nuuly tops 500,000 subscribers as inventory expands to 33,000 items
item.description:
Nuuly, the rental service of Urban Outfitters Inc., reported over 500,000 active subscribers and grew its inventory to more than 33,000 items. The platform now carries clothing from more than 500 external brand partners, including Nike, Barbour and J. Crew.
Nuuly offers algorithm-driven sizing and a pause‑and‑cancel feature to simplify the subscriber experience. Behind the front end, the company manages reverse logistics, continuously receiving, cleaning, repairing and re‑shipping each garment. David Hayne, president of Nuuly and chief technology officer of URBN, said the service aims to give women an affordable way to refresh their wardrobes.
“There’s a tension there between the desire for newness and the desire for variety, and then what it costs,” David Hayne, president of Nuuly and chief technology officer of URBN said.
“At the end of the day, Nuuly is a platform that helps drive brand awareness,” David Hayne, president of Nuuly and chief technology officer of URBN said.
Urban Outfitters Inc. introduced Nuuly as a subscription rental option as consumers questioned the financial and environmental impact of constantly buying new clothing.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/how-smart-logistics-tech-is-scaling-rentals-nuuly-urbn-1239259328)

item.title: East Coast Asia-US container rates hold at $9,600
item.description:
Last week, East Coast Asia-US container spot rates held steady at about $9,600 per forty-foot equivalent unit while West Coast rates rose 4% to more than $8,100 per FEU. Despite the increase, trans-Pacific rates remain well below the September 2021 peak when Asia-West Coast prices topped $20,000 per FEU.
The elevated trans-Pacific rates reflect strong U.S.-bound demand, weather-related port congestion in the Far East and carriers managing capacity through blanked sailings. Asia to North Europe spot rates fell 15% last week to about $3,700 per FEU, while Asia-Mediterranean rates dropped 7% to roughly $3,900 per FEU after exceeding $7,000 in July. Carriers are also reducing capacity in anticipation of softer volumes during China’s Golden Week holiday and a broader demand easing expected after the peak season ends in October. A possible indefinite strike at German ports could add to the pressure on Asia-North Europe services. The Verdi labor union is voting on a job action that could begin as early as October, potentially worsening terminal congestion and constraining carrier capacity.
The divergence follows an unusually early east-west peak season that began in May and lifted container spot rates sharply through early July, according to analyst and SONAR data contributor Freightos (NASDAQ: CRGO). Freightos said that the current market is more comparable to the 2024 peak season, when Red Sea diversions constrained effective vessel capacity.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/but-no-pandemic-high-asia-us-container-rate-at-9600)

item.title: PETA protests H&M and COS shows over wool, citing abuse allegations
item.description:
On September 13, two PETA activists stormed the COS runway at New York Fashion Week, and on September 17, three PETA supporters did the same at H&M’s London Fashion Week show. The disruption led to the resignation of Steven Kolb, then chief executive and president of the Council of Fashion Designers of America, after two decades in the role. PETA says its campaign targets H&M Group’s use of NATIVA‑certified wool, which it claims is linked to animal abuse.
NATIVA, created by Chargeurs Luxury Materials, certifies wool sourced from farms in Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, North America, Uruguay and Argentina and employs blockchain to trace the fibre from farm to consumer. PETA alleges that an undercover investigation at a South African wool operation it says was NATIVA‑certified showed workers kicking sheep, striking them with shearing equipment and a piece of wood, dragging lambs by their legs and cutting animals during shearing. The organisation also reported finding a lamb with a maggot‑infested wound and a dead lamb during that investigation. H&M responded that animal welfare is “very important” to it and that no animal should be harmed to make its products.
“These protests highlight that every wool garment is a product of suffering,” Ingrid Newkirk, PETA founder said.
PETA says its current campaign is focused on H&M Group and the use of wool that it alleges is obtained through animal rights abuses. The charity’s campaign intensified after a PETA Asia undercover investigation at a South African wool operation that, according to PETA, was NATIVA‑certified and connected to H&M Group’s supply chain.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/peta-hm-cos-wool)

item.title: Tesco pilots virtual try-on for 1,500 F&F items at Sandhurst Extra store
item.description:
Tesco has launched a pilot of virtual try-on technology for 1,500 F&F clothing items at its Sandhurst Extra store. The trial is part of a broader refresh of the F&F offering that adds new changing rooms, a dedicated service hub and an expanded in‑store range, while Tesco also rolls out hundreds of extra styles online.
Shoppers can upload or take a photo of themselves on a digital screen and then select a digital model to see how garments look in different sizes. In addition to the virtual try‑on, the Sandhurst Extra store features updated lighting, new signage and a larger F&F selection across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear, plus clearer homeware displays. Online, Tesco has broadened its fashion catalogue with hundreds of additional styles, more size options and exclusive ranges, supported by improved search tools and curated styling inspiration.
Tesco first introduced its online fashion offer last year, which it described as successful, and is now expanding that digital assortment alongside the in‑store trial.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/tesco-trials-virtual-try-on)

item.title: Amazon adds eBay, Shopify, TikTok, Walmart links to Seller Central
item.description:
Amazon today launched multichannel selling tools in Seller Central that let sellers manage sales across Amazon, eBay, Shopify, TikTok and Walmart, a move aimed at the more than 95% of independent sellers who already sell on multiple channels, and the tools are free to use. The tools let sellers create and edit listings once, with changes automatically formatted for each channel’s requirements, view combined sales and profitability data, arrange fulfillment from Seller Central, and adjust pricing or inventory, manage returns, and track advertising performance, without leaving the dashboard.
Sellers easily start by visiting the multichannel settings page in Seller Central’s top‑right navigation bar, then click to connect their eBay, Shopify, TikTok or Walmart accounts. Connected data stays private and accessible only to the seller, who can import existing listings, link them to Amazon‑catalog products, and later disconnect any channel at will. Sellers can see combined order queues, print shipping labels, and track returns from a single dashboard, eliminating the need to log into each marketplace separately. The tools also sync inventory levels in real time, so a sale on one channel automatically reduces stock across all connected platforms, preventing overselling.
“We really believe that when sellers succeed across their entire business, they’re going to succeed on Amazon as well,” David Forsythe, Amazon’s VP of North America seller business said.
Amazon began its multichannel effort years ago after sellers said managing inventory across multiple places was a significant challenge. The company responded by launching Multichannel Fulfillment, Amazon Warehousing and Distribution, and Buy with Prime to create a unified inventory pool.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/small-business/amazon-seller-central-multichannel-selling-tools)

item.title: Amazon launches tools to cut global seller costs by up to 60%
item.description:
Amazon announced new tools that enable sellers to list a product once and sell in up to eight countries by year-end. Sellers active in more than one country earn 70% more revenue on average than those selling in just one.
The new compliance tools let sellers test a product once and receive certification valid in multiple countries, with early pilot participants reporting savings of up to 60%. Global Warehousing and Distribution will expand from the United States to eight countries by the end of the year, offering storage costs up to 45% lower than the existing U.S.-based Amazon Warehousing and Distribution service. A unified seller dashboard, introduced this fall, shows demand and economics across the United States, Europe and Japan, with additional countries to be added by year-end, and will eventually let sellers manage listings, inventory and orders in one place.
Amazon already reaches more rural U.S. shoppers than before, and it notes that only about three in ten sellers currently list products internationally. The company says the main hurdle is having to manage separate inventory, compliance, listings and logistics for each country.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-sellers-global-expansion-tools)

item.title: Lowe’s launches 20‑minute drone delivery in Matthews, NC with Wing and DoorDash
item.description:
Lowe’s has launched a drone delivery pilot in Matthews, North Carolina, offering 20‑minute delivery of select home improvement items through Wing and DoorDash. The pilot covers more than 100 SKUs, ranging from hand tools to paint supplies.
Customers place orders via the DoorDash app, and Wing drones pick up the items from Lowe’s store and fly them to the customer’s location. The service is limited to a curated list of eligible products, including all‑purpose cleaner, caulk, hand tools, household batteries, painter’s tape, screwdrivers and soap. Lowe’s uses its physical stores as hubs for staging drone dispatch areas, integrating DoorDash’s marketplace demand into the drone workflow. The pilot adds to Lowe’s existing same‑day options such as BOPIS, curbside pickup and same‑day delivery.
“By piloting drone delivery, we’re addressing a real project pain point with an innovative solution that is integrated into the retail journey, giving our hometown customers next‑generation fulfillment right when they need it,” Seemantini Godbole, chief information and AI officer at Lowe’s said.
Lowe’s pointed to its AI assistants Mylow and Mylow Companion, which together have answered more than 25 million questions since launching in 2025. The retailer also noted its No. 9 position in the Top 1000 Database and No. 90 in Digital Commerce 360’s new AI Rankings.
Source: Digital Commerce 360 (https://digitalcommerce360.com/2026/09/24/lowes-launches-drone-delivery-partnership-wing-doordash)

item.title: Amazon lets U.S. merchants add free Prime delivery to their sites at no extra cost
item.description:
Amazon now lets U.S. merchants add fast, free Prime delivery to their own websites at no extra cost, with setup 70% faster on average than enabling standalone Buy with Prime. Early adopters have seen over 40% of their eligible orders shipped with Prime delivery.
Merchants can enable the option through the Amazon MCF and Buy with Prime app for Shopify, or via Amazon's Selling Partner API and upcoming integrations with partners like Fulfil, LingXing, and WebBee. When shoppers select Prime delivery at checkout, Amazon verifies their Prime membership and fulfills the order from the merchant's inventory using its logistics network. Order confirmation and tracking are provided directly by the merchant, while the Prime badge appears on product pages to signal the benefit.
“Since enabling it, we've seen a nearly 10% increase in sales, orders go out in about a day and a half, and ‘where is my order?’ inquiries have nearly disappeared,” Gabriella Luksander, general manager at Skinnies Instant Lifts said.
Merchants can turn it on in minutes, with setup 70% faster on average compared to enabling standalone Buy with Prime, and no changes to payments processing, order management, or store policies. Merchants who use Amazon's fulfillment network to ship orders from their own websites can now offer their shoppers something new at checkout: fast, free Prime delivery.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-mcf-prime-delivery-merchant-websites)

item.title: Lidl faces ban on Birkenstock lookalikes in Netherlands after court injunction
item.description:
Lidl faces a €5,000 daily penalty after a Dutch court ordered it to stop selling Birkenstock lookalikes in the Netherlands. The injunction covers Birkenstock’s Arizona, Madrid, Gizeh, Boston and Florida sandal designs.
Lidl must pay €5,000 (about £4,200) for each day it continues to sell the prohibited models. The retailer must also give Birkenstock full details of sales and orders for the affected sandals. Lidl will have to compensate Birkenstock for damages and cover its legal costs, with amounts to be set later. The court said the infringement relates mainly to the distinctive footbed design used across Birkenstock’s footwear.
In November 2025 a Dutch court ordered Scapino to stop selling several Birkenstock lookalikes, a decision that is still under appeal. The Court of Justice of the European Union ruled in December that industrially designed products can qualify for copyright protection when they reflect the creator’s own intellectual creation. Earlier in 2025 Germany’s highest civil court found Birkenstock’s sandals to be functional rather than copyright‑protected works of art.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/lidl-banned-from-selling-birkenstock-lookalikes-after-copyright-ruling)

item.title: Sephora starts TikTok Shop with Mikayla Nogueira livestream
item.description:
Sephora launched its TikTok Shop on Saturday with a livestream hosted by Mikayla Nogueira, selling close to 2,300 products so far. The launch featured an exclusive 12‑piece POV Beauty holiday set advertised at a $327 value for $265.
Sephora’s TikTok Shop currently offers only POV Beauty and Sephora Collection items. The retailer plans to add new products on a monthly drop‑model basis. According to NielsenIQ, TikTok Shop is the fourth‑largest health and beauty retailer in the U.S., with sales exceeding $4.4 billion since its 2023 U.S. launch.
“Do these retailers want to go to TikTok Shop? They would prefer that the world comes to their own domain, and they can control that experience. But the world doesn’t really work that way,” Blaine Nielsen, president of retailers at e-commerce agency Rithum said.
Sephora had offered the POV Beauty holiday set since September, with the product page directing shoppers to its newly launched TikTok Shop. In July, Ulta Beauty joined TikTok Shop with a perfume launch featuring Ice Spice.
Source: Modern Retail (https://modernretail.co/marketing/how-sephora-used-mikayla-nogueira-and-pov-beauty-to-kickstart-its-tiktok-shop-launch)

item.title: Amazon expands US pickup network to nearly 30,000 locations
item.description:
Amazon now offers nearly 30,000 pickup locations across the United States. Customers are on track to collect more than 100 million packages from these sites this year. Most U.S. customers have a pickup location within five miles of home.
Shoppers can choose Amazon Lockers, Whole Foods Market stores or other participating sites during checkout. Once a package arrives, Amazon emails a pickup code or barcode with the address and location details.
“We want customers to be able to get their Amazon packages in the way that works best for them,” Viraj Chatterjee, vice president of Amazon Transportation said.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-pickup-locations-expansion)

item.title: Amazon adds persistent memory and Quick-Claude plugin to Seller Assistant
item.description:
Amazon today added persistent memory and a new Quick-Claude plugin to Seller Assistant, which now reaches over 90% of Amazon’s selling partners worldwide. The update also includes a free 12-month Quick Plus subscription for sellers using the new plugin. The assistant retains a long-term record of each seller’s pricing trends, stock cycles, and growth targets, accessible whether they work in Seller Central, Quick or Claude.
Workflows let sellers automate routine tasks such as restocking and price changes, with full audit trails and seller-defined guardrails. The plugin brings Seller Assistant’s AI into Amazon Quick and a beta version of Anthropic’s Claude, allowing sellers to query their business data through natural conversation.
Amazon launched Seller Assistant in 2023 as a generative AI tool to answer questions and surface insights for sellers. After sellers said they wanted more automation, Amazon added agentic capabilities that let the assistant reason, plan, and act on a seller’s behalf.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/seller-assistant-plugin-amazon-quick-claude)

item.title: Amazon, Stella McCartney, and Canopy launch Fashion Coalition with 60+ signatories
item.description:
Today Amazon, Stella McCartney, and Canopy announced the launch of the Climate Pledge Fashion Coalition, which already has over 60 signatories The coalition aims to help its members reach net-zero carbon emissions by 2040
The coalition will align demand across signatories to create blended financing mechanisms that pair development‑finance de‑risking with private capital, helping innovators price sustainable materials closer to mainstream levels. Through its Fashion Coalition Lever Library, members access over 100 proven and emerging options, and fiber‑by‑fiber guidance, while the coalition also uses Next Gen Now, a Canopy‑led initiative, to link signatories with innovative materials ready for commercial adoption. By showing that production‑stage innovations can work at scale, the coalition provides policymakers with real‑world evidence for smarter environmental policy, countering the industry’s estimated 2 to 8% of global carbon emissions, 79 trillion liters of water use, and 92 million tons of annual textile waste. Innovators receive long‑term volume commitments that enable price parity with incumbent fibers, while the coalition’s scaled sustainable materials bring more sustainable fashion choices to customers at every price point
“Through The Climate Pledge, we're bringing together more than 60 fashion and retail brands, manufacturers, and innovators to help make that happen,” Kara Hurst, chief sustainability officer at Amazon said.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/sustainability/amazon-climate-pledge-sustainability-fashion-coalition)

item.title: Amazon explains how 28 years of AWS experience shaped its custom chip designs
item.description:
At the AI Infra Summit on September 16, Amazon senior vice president Peter DeSantis said the company’s 28‑year history with AWS has guided its custom silicon development from Nitro to Graviton to Trainium. He noted that today the vast majority of workloads on AWS run both faster and more cost‑effective on Graviton processors.
The Nitro System moved the virtualization stack onto dedicated hardware, allowing customers to get bare‑metal performance simply by launching an EC2 instance. Graviton processors were developed using internal workload data from Amazon’s own services and customer applications rather than relying on generic benchmarks. Trainium chips were shaped by close work with leading AI customers, and their hardware‑enabled profiler captures fine‑grained telemetry from production workloads without interference. DeSantis highlighted that memory bandwidth often determines how fast a generative model can produce responses, making it a key focus for AI chip design.
“When you're building hardware and building complex systems, understanding the workload deeply is a huge asset,” Peter DeSantis, senior vice president of foundational AI models and custom silicon said.
Amazon now designs chips for networking, general‑purpose computing, and AI, but the company did not set out to become a chip designer. As DeSantis explained, each step in its silicon journey began with a customer workload that needed something better than existing hardware could provide.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/peter-desantis-amazon-ai-chips-design)

item.title: Amazon asks Meta to remove its store from Muse AI agent experience
item.description:
Amazon asked Meta to remove its storefront from the Muse AI agent experience two weeks after the assistant launched and saw Meta’s shares climb 11%. The request follows Meta’s launch of Muse, an AI agent that can shop and pay on behalf of users without identifying itself.
Amazon said it was not given advance notice that Muse would access its online store and did not authorize the agent. The company said Muse does not identify itself when browsing and appears to capture and store shopper credentials. Amazon cited a need for third‑party applications to operate openly and respect retailers’ decisions about participation. The move echoes Amazon’s earlier legal action against Perplexity’s Comet AI agent, which is still pending after a U.S. appeals court overturned a temporary ban in August. Shopify announced it will enable Muse for agentic checkouts across all its stores using Shop Pay.
“We think it’s fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate,” Lara Hendrickson, Amazon spokesperson said.
In April, Meta signed a deal with Amazon Web Services to use its chips for agentic AI. Amazon has previously blocked Perplexity’s Comet AI agent from accessing its site and is currently litigating that case. Earlier this year Amazon piloted its own “Buy for Me” feature, which lets shoppers buy from external sellers through Amazon’s platform.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/amazon-meta-muse-ai-agent-shopping-experience/831018)

item.title: Gap launches multiyear 'fashiontainment' strategy with boy band Just Your Type
item.description:
Gap has launched a multiyear 'fashiontainment' strategy featuring a partnership with boy band Just Your Type. The partnership notes that Just Your Type has generated more than 450 million views over the past three months. Gap will also roll out a fall capsule collection with the musicians and host fan experiences at malls across the United States.
As part of the deal, Gap will co‑produce a documentary series that offers a look at the band’s live performances, creative process and each of the five members’ personalities. Gap has also developed a fall capsule collection with the musicians and plans to host fan experiences at malls around the United States. The collaboration will include additional social content and activations to support cultural storytelling, using Gap’s brick‑and‑mortar footprint.
“With JYT, we're drawing on the full breadth of Gap — from creative storytelling and fashion to our stores and experiences — to give audiences multiple ways into the band's world,” Pam Kaufman, chief entertainment officer, Gap Inc said.
The news offers an early sign of what to expect from Gap Inc.’s Fashiontainment platform, which it began ramping up this year. The company in January hired former Paramount executive Pam Kaufman as its first chief entertainment officer and has steadily built out the division since. Lourdes Arocho, another Paramount alum, was appointed senior vice president and head of licensing in May while Gap Inc. last month brought on Justin Breton as vice president of development from Walmart.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/gap-rolls-out-fashiontainment-strategy-with-boy-band-collaboration/831023)

item.title: Rhine water at 16 cm below threshold chokes barge traffic
item.description:
The Rhine River’s water level in its shallowest middle section dropped to 16 centimeters below the low-water threshold as of Monday, threatening to halt barge traffic on a key central Europe corridor. As of Monday, the river’s navigable depth measured roughly 4.25 feet, per Germany’s Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration.
The river connects the Rotterdam and Antwerp ports—handling 14.2 million and 13.6 million TEU annually—to inland cities across Europe. Only very small vessels or barges loaded to no more than 20 % of capacity can navigate the upper and middle Rhine, per terminal operator Oliver Haas. One barge typically moves the freight of about 200 trucks, so the capacity shortfall is pushing shippers onto rail and road networks that lack spare trains, terminal space and drivers. Rail bottlenecks at the North Sea ports and a shortage of truck drivers are adding to delays and raising costs for container repositioning and demurrage. The Elbe and Danube rivers are also experiencing historically low water levels due to severe drought and heat.
“The only very small vessels, or ones partially loaded to 20% of their capacity, are able to transit the upper and middle Rhine,” Oliver Haas, general manager of HGK Intermodal, a terminal operator at the Port of Cologne said.
Conditions have only gotten worse in the past month. Previous low-water events in Europe have typically occurred in late summer or fall, when dry summers followed low snow melts, so experts are unsure what to predict with rivers drying out so early.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/record-low-rhine-levels-choke-barge-traffic-stress-ground-transport)

item.title: Amazon puts $1.9 billion into DSP program to lift driver pay to almost $24/hour
item.description:
Amazon said it will invest an additional $1.9 billion in its Delivery Service Partner program in 2027. The investment is expected to help DSP owners raise driver pay to a national average of nearly $24 per hour. At the same time, Amazon reported that serious vehicle crashes across its DSP network fell more than 23% last year.
Amazon will also allocate $70 million over the next five years to community impact initiatives led by DSP owners. By the end of this year, surround‑view camera technology will be installed in half of the Rivian electric delivery vehicles used by DSPs. The company is rolling out AI‑powered tools such as Wellspring and Smart Delivery Glasses to improve route accuracy and delivery speed. Navigation in the Amazon Delivery App will now automatically adjust routes during bad weather or when hazards are detected, without driver intervention.
Since 2022, Amazon has invested more than $543 million in safety initiatives and technology for DSP owners. Over the past three years, those investments have helped DSP owners increase driver pay by an average of 16% nationwide. The DSP program’s annual Ignite Live conference in Las Vegas brings together thousands of owners to share updates and celebrate achievements.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/transportation/amazon-dsp-program-investment-2026)

item.title: Australian adaptive-fashion label JAM the Label ceases operations after nearly nine years
item.description:
JAM the Label, the Australian adaptive-fashion brand founded by Molly Rogers and Emma Clegg, is closing its doors after almost nine years in business. The shutdown highlights the struggle of adaptive apparel founders who must build both a product line and a market unfamiliar with the category.
The label had been stocked by The Iconic since 2021, when the retailer added JAM to its adaptive edit alongside two other brands, marking one of the label’s first major retail partnerships. Between 2022 and 2024, JAM showcased collections at Melbourne Fashion Week and Melbourne Fashion Festival, gaining visibility on runways that highlighted its adaptive designs to industry audiences. At its peak, The Iconic’s adaptive edit featured more than 130 pieces from JAM, Christina Stephens and Tommy Hilfiger, offering consumers a broad selection of adaptive clothing options. Founders cited prolonged sampling processes, higher production costs for specialised designs, and the ongoing need to educate retailers and consumers as key obstacles, noting that extra difficulty often emerged during prototyping with elements such as zip direction or magnet strength affecting functionality.
“Around 1 in 5 people in Australia identify as living with disability,” Molly Rogers, co-founder said.
“They add three zeros to it,” Emma Clegg, co-founder said.
Before its closure, JAM had gained early mainstream recognition when The Iconic included it in the inaugural Adaptive Edit of 2021. The brand also appeared at major Australian fashion events, including Melbourne Fashion Week and Melbourne Fashion Festival, from 2022 through 2024.
Source: Inside Retail Asia (https://insideretail.asia/2026/09/21/why-the-fashion-market-failed-jam-the-label)

item.title: Three major central banks raise rates, signaling further hikes
item.description:
The Bank of Japan raised rates on Friday, the Federal Reserve did so two days earlier and the European Central Bank lifted rates last week, marking three major central bank tightening moves. Fed projections show policymakers expect a 4.25‑4.50 percent policy rate range by the end of 2027.
Updated quarterly economic projections showed 16 of 18 Federal Reserve policymakers anticipate at least one more quarter‑percentage‑point increase by the end of this year. The Bank of England kept its rate unchanged this week but warned that inflation pressures could require further action. ECB Vice President Boris Vujcic told Reuters that energy prices are expected to stay elevated for longer and that future policy decisions will be made on a meeting‑by‑meeting basis. JPMorgan’s Greg Fuzesi said the peak in rates remains uncomfortably dependent on Middle East events, noting that a hike above 3 percent cannot be ruled out.
“Our policy phase has changed,” Kazuo Ueda, Governor of the Bank of Japan said.
“The peak in rates is uncomfortably dependent on events in the Middle East; a hike above 3 per cent cannot be ruled out entirely,” Greg Fuzesi, JPMorgan said.
A month ago, a short‑lived pact between the United States and Iran had encouraged investors and policymakers to bet on easing hostilities and a retreat of energy prices. The breakdown of the US‑Iran accord and the Houthi advance along the Red Sea have worsened the outlook for oil supplies.
Source: Inside Retail Asia (https://insideretail.asia/2026/09/21/why-central-banks-are-bracing-for-further-rate-rises)

item.title: Oxford Report Says Fashion Influences 30% of Global Farmland
item.description:
The University of Oxford’s Smith School estimates that fashion’s fiber sourcing influences about 30.15 percent of global agricultural land. Leather and wool together account for nearly 97 percent of that total, with leather linked to 876 million hectares and wool to 528.4 million hectares.
Cotton accounts for 34.7 million hectares, while linen and hemp cover 5.9 million hectares and silk 2.3 million hectares. The report’s methodology counts the full agricultural footprint of each fiber, even when the same land also produces food or other commodities, to gauge the influence fashion brands could exert through purchasing. In 2024, more than 2.9 billion square meters of genuine leather were processed worldwide, of which footwear, handbags and apparel used 1.2 billion square meters. Even without wool, the remaining fiber categories would still touch roughly 19 percent of global farmland, with leather alone representing 18.25 percent. The report also notes that apparel absorbs roughly half of global fiber production, with home textiles taking another quarter and industrial, technical, medical and other uses making up the remainder.
“We are not measuring blame. We are measuring power, and it turns out fashion has far more of it than anyone has been telling us,” Arizona Muse, Dirt’s founder and one of the report’s authors said.
“A brand changing how it sources is changing how land is farmed,” Sam Fankhauser, director of the Smith School and another of the report’s authors said.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sustainability/oxford-fashion-farmland-leather-wool-biodynamic-1239245351)

item.title: Shopify’s EMEA managing director Deann Evans departs after five years
item.description:
Deann Evans announced her departure as Shopify’s managing director for EMEA after five years in the role. She said she had spent the past four weeks away from work weighing her next move, without naming a future employer. She noted that Shopify now serves everyone from first‑time founders to some of the world’s largest enterprises in Europe.
Before Shopify, Evans worked at GoToDigital, Mettrr and Sizmek. Under her leadership, the company’s partner ecosystem expanded and new products were brought to merchants across the region. According to Retail Technology Innovation Hub, the Shopify catalogue contains more than one billion products structured for discovery, and Evans said AI is reshaping how merchants sell. She thanked her team, partners and merchants, saying their talent will continue to drive Shopify’s success in Europe.
“Over the past four weeks, I’ve had the opportunity to step back, spend valuable time with my family, and reflect on what comes next,” Deann Evans, former Managing Director, EMEA, Shopify said.
“With more than one billion products structured for discovery in the Shopify Catalogue and partnerships opening new ways to sell across major AI platforms Shopify is helping merchants of every size embrace the future of commerce,” Deann Evans, former Managing Director, EMEA, Shopify said.
Evans joined Shopify five years ago after roles at GoToDigital, Mettrr and Sizmek. During her tenure, she helped shift the company’s perception in Europe from a platform for small businesses to one serving large enterprises and pointed to growth in the partner ecosystem and new merchant products.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/shopifys-managing-director-for-emea-deann-evans-departs-after-five-years-without-disclosing-where-she-goes-next)

item.title: eBay overhauls leadership, policies and fees amid executive departure
item.description:
eBay announced the departure of VP Blair Ethington after nearly four years, while promoting Dr. Saskia Meier-Andrae to lead its European Union operations, updating seller policies effective September and October, and noting changes to its UK fitment tools. Starting October 15, eBay will exclude livestream sales from its Seller Standards, Service Metrics and Top Rated Plus programs, meaning those transactions no longer affect fee discounts or surcharges.
The company also warned that USPS shipping rates accessed through eBay Labels will rise again on September 19, with the notice issued just one day before the increase takes effect. In the United Kingdom, eBay has launched Fitment Plus Auto, a tool that integrates vehicle fitment data directly into listings, as it prepares to retire the standalone myFitment service later this month. Additionally, eBay’s Australian site is expanding its Authenticity Guarantee to cover watches, offering both mandatory and buyer‑paid authentication options. The new VP & General Manager Europe role, filled by Dr. Saskia Meier-Andrae, aims to streamline cross‑border transactions and harmonize seller support across the bloc.
The briefing noted that rival livestream platform Whatnot has criticized eBay’s new Live fee structure while adjusting its own commission model for top sellers. It also mentioned that eBay is seeking expertise to shape the long‑term economics of its Shipping Protections program as it assumes greater liability for package issues.
Source: Value Added Resource (https://valueaddedresource.net/week-in-review-9-20-26)

item.title: Tesla plans 538,720‑square‑foot Texas distribution center
item.description:
Tesla filed plans Sept. 1 for a 538,720‑square‑foot distribution center near Austin, Texas. The facility is slated for completion on Dec. 4, 2028.
The project covers 538,720 square feet and carries an estimated construction cost of $1.44 million. Work is scheduled to begin Dec. 7 and be completed Dec. 4, 2028, according to the state filing. The filing describes the project as a “new lease space build‑out for Tesla in the existing Office/WHSE building” at Mustang Ridge Distribution Center I, located at 6925 FM Road 1327 in Mustang Ridge. The filing does not specify what products or materials Tesla will handle at the distribution center or how many employees will work there.
The project represents another expansion of Tesla’s operations in Central Texas, where the company has established Austin as its corporate headquarters and operates its large Gigafactory Texas manufacturing complex. Tesla already draws components from an extensive supplier network in Mexico, with suppliers in Nuevo León, Coahuila, Tamaulipas, Chihuahua, the Bajío region, and the state of Mexico shipping automotive components north to the Texas factory.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/borderlands-mexico-tesla-plans-massive-texas-distribution-center)

item.title: J.B. Hunt warns of 5%‑10% Q3 earnings hit as diesel prices surge
item.description:
Last week, J.B. Hunt warned that rising fuel and driver costs could cut its third‑quarter earnings by 5% to 10%. Retail diesel prices climbed about 31% between July 5 and September 17, while wholesale prices rose more than twice as fast.
Because many large carriers buy fuel at wholesale rates and pass costs to customers via retail‑based fuel surcharges, a narrowing wholesale‑retail spread erodes their margin buffer. The fuel spread has fallen to just above $1 per gallon since early July, down from roughly $1.25 averaged from 2022 through March and above $1.50 from April to July. Smaller fleets that lack wholesale purchasing power face a different squeeze, with retail diesel up about 24% over the past three months while spot rates have slipped roughly 6%. In a competitive market, smaller fleets struggle to pass higher retail diesel costs through spot rates, limiting their ability to raise prices.
Most of J.B. Hunt’s dedicated and intermodal contracts were set before the market flip in late 2025 and early 2026, leaving them exposed to operating‑cost inflation. The market viewed the warning as a giveback after a potentially bloated second quarter, not a long‑term threat.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/fuel-cost-spike-hits-carrier-margins)

item.title: USPS Loses $3.1 Billion to Counterfeit Labels Over Two Years
item.description:
The U.S. Postal Service lost an estimated $3.1 billion to counterfeit package labels between March 2024 and February 2026, according to a new Inspector General audit. The audit also found that approximately 2 million paid packages were mistakenly routed for extra processing from December 2024 through February 2026 because of processing or mail-entry errors.
Postal Service tracking data showed that 97 percent of counterfeit labels were still processed for delivery from October 2023 through February 2026, indicating limited success of interception systems. Counterfeit labels alone caused an estimated $1.6 billion loss in fiscal year 2025, when USPS generated $32.6 billion from shipping 6.8 billion packages. The OIG estimates the agency could lose another $520 million through February 2028 if current trends continue, raising the total potential impact to more than $3.6 billion over four years. An internal USPS analysis of April 2026 volume attributed 47 percent of the mistaken‑package errors to employees or technology and 52 percent to customers failing to transmit payment records before entering packages into the mailstream.
Earlier reports in April noted that online sellers were seeing packages rejected at drop‑off as “unpaid” as USPS rolled out stricter postage‑verification measures. The September 10 Inspector General report expands on those earlier observations by providing a broader view of the counterfeit‑label problem and its financial impact.
Source: Value Added Resource (https://valueaddedresource.net/usps-counterfeit-label-oig-report)

item.title: Fake FedEx drivers steal $680,000 electronics load from New Castle warehouse
item.description:
On Sept. 14, two men posing as FedEx employees picked up a $680,000 electronics shipment from a New Castle, DE, warehouse using fraudulent documents. Delaware State Police arrested Dushatdaman Parihar, 35, of Manteca, CA, the next day and recovered the intact trailer at a Newark parking area.
The suspects presented driver’s licenses and shipping paperwork that described the electronics as valued above $680,000, then hooked the trailer to their tractor‑trailer cab and drove away. After the business realized the documents were fake, it located the trailer at University Plaza in Newark and alerted police. When officers arrived, Parihar approached the vehicle and was found with false credentials and a fraudulent registration plate. Police returned the untouched trailer and its cargo to the warehouse and charged Parihar with multiple felonies, setting a $66,550 secured bond at his arraignment.
“Detective S. Marioni accepts information at 302-365-8388,” Detective S. Marioni said.
The case began with a pickup near Wilmington, DE. Investigators connected the scheme to fraudulent identification, shipping records and a false registration plate.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/fake-fedex-drivers-steal-680k-electronics-load-from-new-castle-de-warehouse)

item.title: YardFlow expands yard automation to over 200 facilities of a beverage giant
item.description:
YardFlow is rolling out its yard‑automation platform to every one of a beverage maker’s 200‑plus sites, building on an earlier 26‑site pilot. The shipper reported moving nearly 5% more freight with the same workforce after the initial deployment, according to YardFlow’s analysis.
YardFlow says its system has processed close to 2 million shipments across the original 26 sites. The platform operates at three‑nines, or 99.9% uptime, the company said. The rollout proceeds from the beverage giant’s largest facilities down to its smallest, aiming for standardized operations across all locations. Drivers check in via QR code or a web portal and need not download an app, a design choice meant to avoid connectivity issues.
“That’s tens of millions of dollars of incremental profit,” Jake Koppinger, founder of YardFlow said.
“They’re pushing us into all of their 200+ facilities, including their smallest, so biggest to smallest, because they want to see that standardization,” Jake Koppinger, founder of YardFlow said.
YardFlow began by addressing the manual bill‑of‑lading process that still relies on paper, staplers and a window slot in thousands of U.S. distribution centers. When the paperwork is misfiled, it creates a cash‑flow problem that surfaces roughly 60 days later as disputed lump‑sum payments.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/yard-flow-200-site-yard-automation-deal)

item.title: eBay VP Blair Ethington to depart on September 18 after nearly four years
item.description:
eBay is losing VP Buyer, Seller & C2C Blair Ethington, who announced her last day will be September 18 after nearly four years in her second stint at the company. She first returned to eBay in January 2023 to lead Focus Categories and Buyer Experience before her role expanded to include Live Shopping and Community in July 2025 and then the broader Buyer, Seller & C2C portfolio in November 2025.
Prior to her return, Ethington worked at eBay as a Senior Product Manager from 2006 to 2010, then held positions at CrowdStar, Sam's Club and Meta.
Ethington's first stint at eBay ran from 2006 to 2010 as a Senior Product Manager before she left for roles at CrowdStar, Sam's Club and Meta.
Source: Value Added Resource (https://valueaddedresource.net/ebay-vp-blair-ethington-departs)

item.title: Burglary hits moving BNSF train, sparking container fire in Riverside
item.description:
Burglars broke into a moving BNSF freight train near Riverside, California, early Thursday, prompting a fire that drew 19 firefighters to the scene. The blaze was brought under control by 5:30 a.m., with no injuries or evacuations reported.
The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago when crews located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets after initial reports placed it west of downtown. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer, with Colton Fire Department also responding. Firefighters extinguished the blaze and recorded control at 5:30 a.m., and the incident was logged as RIV #26-34784. BNSF Police are leading the investigation into the burglary and fire, though no suspects, arrests, vehicles, losses or service disruptions have been identified.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/burglary-hits-moving-bnsf-train-as-container-catches-fire-in-riverside)

item.title: Trump-Xi summit may delay new 7.5% Section 301 tariffs on 16 U.S. trading partners
item.description:
President Donald Trump’s summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday may postpone a planned tranche of Section 301 tariffs that would affect 16 U.S. trading partners, including China. The administration had aimed to publish a report recommending a 7.5% duty on Chinese goods before the meeting, but now the release is uncertain.
The investigation, which began in March, targets countries accused of excess capacity, adding to an existing 12.5% duty on Chinese imports tied to forced labor that took effect on July 24.
“China engages in normal economic and trade cooperation with other countries on the basis of equality and mutual benefit. Such cooperation does not target any third party and shall be free from disruption or coercion from any third party,” China Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said during his daily briefing,” Guo Jiakun, spokesman for China’s Foreign Ministry said.
The Section 301 investigation was launched in March to address alleged excess capacity in 16 economies, including China and the European Union.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/trade/section-301-excess-capacity-tariffs-delay-trump-xi-summit-1239245815)

item.title: eBay warns sellers of USPS rate hikes effective September 19, 2026 with one day's notice
item.description:
eBay announced on September 18, 2026 that USPS shipping rates available through eBay Labels will increase effective September 19, 2026, giving sellers just one day's notice. Ground Advantage rates will rise $0.10 for packages weighing 0‑2 pounds and from $0.27 to $2.28 for 3‑5‑pound parcels across Zones 1‑8, while Priority Mail flat‑rate packages will go up $0.30 for the same zones.
The adjustments do not apply to rural ZIP Codes, which keep a separate USPS rate structure that has been in place since 2024. eBay’s shipping calculator will automatically update to reflect the new rates when they take effect on September 19. USPS temporary peak‑season pricing is scheduled to start October 4 and run through January 17, adding another round of changes shortly after the September update. eBay reported double‑digit year‑over‑year growth in shipping revenue for Q2 2026 and cited shipping, advertising and payments as positive contributors to its take rate.
eBay sellers have been dealing with frequent USPS rate changes since a surprise discount in June lowered Ground Advantage costs for 3‑5‑pound shipments. That was followed by revisions to ounce‑based tier pricing for Ground Advantage, the regular annual USPS rate update in July, and several adjustments to specific weights and zones throughout August. USPS temporary peak‑season pricing is set to begin October 4 and run through January 17, meaning another rate shift is due just over two weeks after the September 19 update.
Source: Value Added Resource (https://valueaddedresource.net/ebay-usps-increase-september-2026)

item.title: Office Depot Group rebrands from ODP Group, unifying 40‑year‑old brand across retail and B2B
item.description:
On September 18, 2026, Office Depot Group announced it had rebranded from the ODP Group and retired the ODP Business Solutions name, unifying its 40‑year‑old Office Depot brand across retail stores and B2B distribution. The company also noted that Office Depot ranks No. 24 in the Top 2000 Database of North American online retailers and is the second‑largest retailer in the office supplies category behind Staples.
The new Office Depot Group name will appear on the company’s website, marketing materials and social media channels over the coming weeks. CEO Craig Gunckel said the change returns the company to a legacy brand with more than 40 years of history, which he believes will positively affect employees, customers and long‑time partners. Analysts warned that aligning the B2B unit under the Office Depot name could confuse procurement officers who associate the brand with brick‑and‑mortar retail, potentially limiting perceptions of the firm’s broader distribution capabilities.
“Office Depot is a brand with more than 40 years of history behind it — the kind of recognition that can’t be built overnight, only earned over decades by showing up for our customers, our partners and the communities we serve,” Craig Gunckel, CEO at Office Depot said.
“One big concern is that procurement officers have already built four decades of connotations to the Office Depot brand as a brick‑and‑mortar entity, which could dilute the identity of the company and its perceived areas of expertise,” Alys Reynders, chief marketing officer at Quickbase said.
Previously, the parent company operated under the ODP Group name while its distribution arm was branded ODP Business Solutions. The rebrand consolidates those units under a single Office Depot identity.
Source: Digital Commerce 360 (https://digitalcommerce360.com/2026/09/18/the-odp-group-rebrands-as-office-depot-group-ditches-odp-business-solutions-name)

item.title: Bam releases Any Weather Mac jacket with 95% recycled polyester, no PFAS
item.description:
Bam launched its Any Weather Mac waterproof jacket, which is made of 95 percent recycled polyester and contains no per‑ and polyfluoroalkyl substances. The jacket employs Bam’s Aquaveil technology, which bonds recycled polyester without PFAS, allowing the garment to be recycled intact.
The Any Weather Mac contains about 95 percent recycled polyester, with the metal zip head the only component that is not recycled. Bam has arranged for the U.K.’s Salvation Army Trading Company to take back used jackets and recycle them, preventing landfill disposal. The Aquaveil process, described by the company as a genuine first, creates a waterproof bond that is as strong as the fabric itself. Although the jacket is designed for end‑of‑life recycling, Bam notes that over 90 percent of its activewear already uses nature‑based or recycled fabrics. The jacket is designed to be sustainable from how it’s made to how it’s discarded, aiming to avoid landfill through recycling.
For two decades Bam has been seeking to reduce the environmental footprint of its activewear, aiming to use nature‑based and recycled fabrics in over 90 percent of its output. Other outerwear brands, including Patagonia, have spent nearly two decades trying to eliminate PFAS without sacrificing performance. New York and California have banned any clothing containing PFAS since last year, creating a market deterrent for traditional waterproofing.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/bam-any-weather-mac-pfas-recyclable-forever-chemicals-1239245334)

item.title: Zebra Technologies launches 10‑inch KC401 self‑service kiosk for retail, hospitality, healthcare and manufacturing
item.description:
Zebra Technologies launched the KC401, a 10‑inch self‑service kiosk aimed at retail, hospitality, healthcare and manufacturing environments. The launch comes as over 60 percent of retailers report that shoppers struggle to find products and navigate stores. Only 23 percent of retailers have fully scaled self‑service solutions across their store fleets, while 80 percent plan to invest or expand such technology in the next two years.
The KC401 features a 10‑inch impact‑tested, scratch‑resistant display sealed against dust and liquids. It offers an optional scanner for hands‑free tasks such as price checks, inventory look‑ups, loyalty identification and returns. The kiosk uses the same mounting solutions and infrastructure as Zebra’s existing CC6000 kiosk, allowing current customers to maintain operational continuity. Zebra positions the device for high‑traffic settings in retail, hospitality, healthcare and manufacturing.
“As customer expectations for speed and convenience continue to grow, self-service technology serves as a defining feature of the modern store and other environments. The KC401 provides a versatile, reliable solution for organizations to deliver the seamless, intuitive self-service experiences that their frontline workers and those they serve expect,” James Poulton, senior vice president of enterprise mobile computing at Zebra Technologies said.
Zebra Technologies already sold self‑service kiosks, mobile computers and multipurpose touchscreens, including the CC6000 model. The KC401 builds on that line‑up as the newest addition to the company’s self‑service portfolio.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/zebra-technologies-self-service-kc401-kiosk-1239244941)

item.title: FedEx adds demand surcharges on US imports from Canada, Europe, Latin America
item.description:
FedEx will levy demand surcharges on various import shipments into the United States from Canada, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean starting Monday until further notice. For example, the demand fee on a 40-pound priority shipment from China would rise $22.40 before any fuel surcharges.
Economy services will see the lower rate increases, while express services will face the higher rate increases.
Last year, FedEx imposed a temporary fee on parcel shipments from China, Hong Kong, and the Philippines entering the United States as importers sought to move inventory ahead of new tariffs and the expiration of the de minimis exemption.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/fedex-levies-fees-on-us-imports-from-canada-europe-and-others/830797)

item.title: Nike adds LVMH exec to board, Lycra names new CEO, Target hires Hilton marketing chief
item.description:
Nike appointed Alexandre Arnault to its board, Lycra installed Hua Du as chief executive officer, and Target named Mark Weinstein chief marketing and guest experience officer Weinstein will oversee Target’s customer experience, marketing, culture and community engagement, as well as its retail media network Roundel and online marketplace Target+
Arnault, who works for LVMH’s luxury division, brings experience from the conglomerate’s portfolio of brands such as Louis Vuitton and Dior. Du previously led the global spandex business at Invista and will now steer Lycra’s product development and commercial strategy. Target’s move brings Weinstein back to the retailer after his tenure as global chief marketing officer at Hilton, where he managed 28 brands and the Hilton Honors loyalty program. Before joining Lycra, Du held senior positions at Invista, overseeing global fiber innovation and sustainability initiatives. In his expanded role, Weinstein will also direct Target’s advertising campaigns and manage relationships with external brand partners.
“As we continue writing the next chapter at Target, deepening how we know and engage our guests will be critical to our success,” Fiddelke said,” Target CEO Michael Fiddelke said.
The latest HR moves made by leading textile and apparel companies. Alexandre Arnault joins Nike’s board, Hua Du takes the helm at Lycra and Target recruits Hilton’s marketing chief in a packed week of executive moves.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/shuffle-board-nike-alexandre-arnault-lycra-ceo-target-1239241775)

item.title: Zipline seeks $1 billion funding that would value it at $20 billion
item.description:
Zipline is in talks to raise roughly $1 billion, a round that would value the company at about $20 billion, according to Bloomberg. The FAA proposal under review would allow as many as 220,000 drone deliveries per day from 220 charging stations and 4,400 pickup kiosks across five Texas metros, up from the roughly 30,000 daily flights currently authorized in Dallas‑Fort Worth.
The FAA opened the review last week and is accepting public comments through Oct. 11.
“The proposed rules are very complicated,” acknowledged Mark McKinnon, an aviation attorney at Fox Rothschild who leads the firm’s drone practice,” Mark McKinnon, aviation attorney at Fox Rothschild said.
“You cannot just fly with a fancy drone,” Skou said. “You have to have the infrastructure, or the digital or the air traffic control layer that makes sure that drones are not colliding in the air,” Jesper Skou, cofounder and CEO of Skypuzzler said.
Paradigm invested $200 million in Zipline in March and is reportedly in discussion to lead the new funding round, while Tiger Global Management is considering participating. Earlier this year, Amazon Prime Air said it plans to expand drone delivery to nearly 500 cities and towns by year‑end, Zipline partnered with Uber Eats to start drone deliveries in Dallas and Houston, and DoorDash obtained FAA Part 135 certification to run its own drone air carrier. Walmart continues to expand its work with Wing and Zipline, aiming to reach hundreds of stores.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/logistics/zipline-funding-1-billion-drone-drones-last-mile-delivery-faa-regulations-1239245201)

item.title: GLP-1 drugs cut U.S. food‑and‑beverage truckloads by 2%, FreightWaves says
item.description:
FreightWaves estimates that GLP-1 medications have reduced U.S. food‑and‑beverage truckloads by 2%, or about 2 million loads per year. Data from Walmart’s pharmacy and grocery records indicate that male GLP-1 users’ households buy 10% fewer calories, while female‑user households buy 6% to 8% less. The snack and beverage category is the most visibly affected, with participants noting a softer‑than‑expected summer for beer and soda volumes.
Ryan Schreiber of Metafora said the drugs curb more than appetite, noting that addictive consumption drops as cravings fade. FreightWaves launched a program called FreightWaves Health aimed at making GLP-1 drugs available to truck‑sector employees, saying specifics will be unveiled at its F3 gathering. Panelists noted that the typical driver is now 61 and that long hours behind the wheel exacerbate weight‑related health problems. Only about one‑tenth of Americans currently use GLP-1 drugs, leaving uncertainty about how far demand erosion could go.
“It’s not just food noise,” Schreiber said. “Any addictive type of consumption you tend to lean away from because cravings kind of go away. So you don’t even really think about it anymore,” Ryan Schreiber, Metafora said.
“There’s less alcohol consumption,” he said. “Consumers are consuming less alcohol today,” Don Everhart, Transflo said.
The conversation occurred ahead of FreightWaves’ F3 conference. FreightWaves said it would reveal further information about its FreightWaves Health trucker program at that event.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/whats-broken-in-freight-tech-right-now)

item.title: FreightWaves unveils its 2027 FreightTech100 list of 100 freight technology companies
item.description:
FreightWaves announced its 2027 FreightTech100, recognizing 100 companies selected for innovation across freight and supply chain technology. Over half of the companies on the 2027 list did not appear in the 2026 roster. The list will be celebrated at the inaugural F3 Awards Dinner on Monday, Oct. 26 in Chattanooga.
The FreightTech100 serves as the first stage of the FreightTech Awards process, after which an independent panel of more than 80 industry executives ranks the companies to determine the top 25. The voting process is overseen by accounting firm Henderson, Hutcherson & McCullough. Companies named to the list receive an official winner badge they can display on their websites, email signatures and social channels. Reservations for the F3 Awards Dinner are required by Oct. 10, and seating is limited.
The list is the first stage of the annual FreightTech Awards process. The 2027 class marks the eighth year of the FreightTech Awards.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/freightwaves-announces-the-2027-freighttech100)

item.title: Lytx warns quiet 2026 hurricane outlook masks rising road risk for fleets
item.description:
Lytx’s 2026 Road Safety Report, based on over 341 billion miles driven by 6.3 million commercial drivers, says a below-normal Atlantic hurricane forecast does not mean fewer road dangers. Collisions in construction jumped 28% in 2025, the largest increase among all sectors Lytx monitors.
Inattentiveness rose 168% as a factor in crashes and near‑misses year over year, driven by phone use and eyes off the road. Device‑use coaching sessions grew 40% in 2025, while following‑distance training remained the most‑coached behavior industrywide. Lytx notes fog makes a severe crash nearly three times more likely than normal conditions and that 23% of large‑truck crashes stem from driving too fast for conditions, not just speeding. Near‑collisions fell 23% across every sector even as overall collisions ticked up, suggesting drivers are avoiding close calls but still hitting objects. The shortage of nearly 440,000 construction workers, partly due to data‑center projects paying 30% above average wages, is straining crews left on job sites.
“A mild hurricane forecast is genuinely good news, but it’s the kind of headline that can create a false sense of security,” Brendon Hill, Senior Vice President of Product, Lytx said.
“Risk is always evolving. If it’s not weather, it’s distracted behavior, or a work zone that changes block by block. You need tools that adapt to the situation, not a rulebook that stays fixed no matter what’s happening on the road,” Brendon Hill, Senior Vice President of Product, Lytx said.
The report also notes that near‑collisions dropped 23% across all sectors Lytx tracks, even as overall collisions rose.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/a-quiet-hurricane-season-wont-mean-a-quiet-year-for-road-risk)

item.title: Tulip cuts Shopify setup time to hours with new Integration Builder
item.description:
Tulip this week released its Integration Builder and expanded its Shopify Connector, cutting the time to set up Shopify environments from days or weeks to hours. The Integration Builder provides a visual canvas and reusable components for bi‑directional data links, using AI‑assisted schema discovery and field mapping to adapt to retailers’ existing taxonomies.
The tool lets teams adjust connections as source‑system schemas evolve, reducing maintenance demands and disruption risk. The expanded Shopify Connector now supports multi‑region and Shopify Markets, enabling brands to link regional storefronts to a single Tulip environment while keeping product catalogs, pricing and languages intact. Following its March merger with Salesfloor, Tulip says it serves about 100 enterprise retail clients and over 100,000 sales associates in more than 70 countries. Tulip’s Global 2025 Clienteling Benchmark Report shows that personalized outreach drives 49% more purchases and 63% higher monthly spend per customer, with clienteling conversion rates averaging 11% and top performers reaching 37%.
“shouldn’t have to overhaul their data taxonomy or build custom middleware to give store associates actionable information. Standard connectors are too limited or rigid for enterprise environments, while bespoke engineering can take weeks or months,” Ian Rawlins, CEO of Tulip said.
“simply works with the data structures and connection methods retailers already use, applying visual configuration and AI-assisted tools to make integration faster and more manageable,” Ian Rawlins, CEO of Tulip said.
Before this release, Tulip’s standard connectors required customization or imposed rigid data structures, making integration costly and slow for enterprise retailers.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/tulip-increases-clienteling-capabilities-retailers-shopify-1239244452)

item.title: Asia‑U.S. container spot rates top $11,000, nearing pandemic highs
item.description:
Spot container rates from Asia to the U.S. West Coast hit $7,960 per FEU and East Coast rates reached $11,259 per FEU as of September 17. East Coast rates are just 11.2% below the January 2022 record of $12,683 per FEU, while both trades have risen more than 320% since late February.
Carriers have added 6% to 7% more space on the Far East‑U.S. East Coast lane for September compared with August, aiming to capture revenue while rates stay near historical highs. Xeneta expects another rate increase in early October as shippers rush cargo ahead of China’s Golden Week factory shutdowns. The Far East‑North Europe route rose nearly 85% from pre‑crisis levels to $4,103 per FEU, and the Far East‑Mediterranean lane increased 33.2% to $4,434 per FEU. North Europe‑U.S. East Coast spot rates more than doubled to $2,956 per FEU, showing a smaller but still significant uplift. Rising bunker costs could lift carrier fuel surcharges, potentially pushing Asia‑U.S. rates even closer to the pandemic‑era peaks. Sand noted that carriers are seizing the opportunity while the market is hot, adding capacity ahead of a possible turn in the next two to three weeks. The Hormuz crisis in late February disrupted global shipping markets, triggering the initial rate surge that has since been amplified by strong demand.
“Spot rates from Far East to U.S. West Coast and U.S. East Coast are up 324% and 325% respectively since pre-Hormuz crisis at the end of February,” Peter Sand, chief analyst at Xeneta said.
“We should expect one more freight rate push at the start of October as shippers rush cargo out of Asia ahead of the Golden Week shutdown,” Peter Sand, chief analyst at Xeneta said.
Before the Hormuz crisis in late February, spot rates on Asia‑U.S. lanes were far lower; they have since more than quadrupled. The January 2022 pandemic peak for the East Coast was $12,683 per FEU, and the West Coast peak was $9,699 per FEU. Europe‑Asia trades have also strengthened, though the magnitude of increa
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/asia-us-container-rates-soar-past-11000-near-pandemic-records)

item.title: Gordon Companies Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy
item.description:
Gordon Companies Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Monday in the Western District of New York. The company disclosed estimated assets between $10 million and $50 million and liabilities within a similar range.
It reported having between 200 and 999 estimated creditors, with FedEx and UPS among the 20 creditors holding the largest unsecured claims. Gordon said it paid Vision33 more than $2 million for an ordering and warehouse‑operations system that never performed as promised. Founded in 1977 and still family‑run, the retailer employs about 350 associates and operates over 400,000 square feet of warehouse and distribution space.
“Because Gordon could not fulfill orders at the rate its sales channels required, Gordon was forced to suspend selling on certain marketplace channels, and at least one major retail partner, Target, imposed a one‑week shipping delay on Gordon’s listings,” Gordon said.
Gordon was founded in 1977 and has remained a family‑operated business, with David Gordon serving as president and CEO. The company lists Target, Kohl’s, Home Depot, Walmart, Amazon, Lowe’s and Michaels as retail partners. Earlier this month it filed an amended complaint against Vision33, alleging the SAP reseller’s system failed to handle holiday‑peak order volume.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/christmas-decor-retailer-gordon-companies-files-chapter-11-bankruptcy/830777)

item.title: On signs Kylian Mbappé as it launches into soccer
item.description:
On announced Friday that it has signed soccer superstar Kylian Mbappé, marking the brand’s entry into the sport. Mbappé, who signed with Nike as a child at the start of his career, will help On build its first football line.
Sydney Schertenleib, who joined On last year as an ambassador, will now also work on product development and testing for the new football line. Soccer pundit Thierry Henry, who has worked with On since 2025, has been named the company’s director of football. On plans to lean on lifestyle designs alongside performance gear, given its large focus on fashion, according to Evercore ISI analysts. Jefferies analysts warned that signing Mbappé is no guarantee of success, noting that football consumers tend to buy boots from brands with decades of performance credibility.
Other smaller players like Skechers and New Balance have tried to break into the category with smaller, less splashy endorsements, but have yet to move the needle from a market share standpoint, according to BMO Capital Markets analysts Kelly Crago and Owen Tunstill. On is likely to lean on lifestyle designs alongside performance gear, given its large focus on fashion and the low margins on cleats and licensed fanwear, according to Evercore ISI analysts led by Michael Binetti.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/on-signs-mbappe-schertenleib-soccer-football-nike-adidas/830761)

item.title: Kroger drops Red Bull from shelves as CEO pushes low‑price agenda
item.description:
Kroger removed Red Bull energy drinks from its supermarkets nationwide at the end of August, according to The Cincinnati Enquirer. As of Friday morning, Kroger’s banner sites showed an out‑of‑stock notice promising affordable prices, while its Harris Teeter banner still listed the drink for sale.
Kroger’s website notice told shoppers the drink was unavailable while the retailer works with suppliers to hold down prices. The notice appeared on Kroger’s banner sites after searches for Red Bull returned the out‑of‑stock message. Foran’s pricing approach stems from his years leading Walmart U.S., where the company cultivated a reputation for relentless cost‑cutting. Since becoming Kroger’s chief executive earlier this year, he has repeatedly said holding down prices is a top priority for the chain. On the most recent earnings call, Foran told analysts that Kroger intends to set a high bar for vendors seeking to raise prices. A Kroger spokesperson declined to comment to Grocery Dive on the Red Bull removal. Harris Teeter, another Kroger banner, continued to list Red Bull for sale online despite the removal elsewhere.
Foran spent years as a top executive at Walmart, where the company’s reputation for relentless cost‑cutting shaped his approach to pricing. When he became Kroger’s chief executive earlier this year, he immediately declared that holding down prices would be a top priority and reiterated that stance on the most recent earnings call, saying Kroger intends to set a high bar for vendors seeking to raise prices.
Source: Grocery Dive (https://grocerydive.com/news/the-friday-checkout-kroger-red-bull-pricing/830708)

item.title: FMCSA grants nationwide HOS waiver for fuel haulers through Dec 16
item.description:
The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration announced an immediate nationwide waiver allowing trucks hauling motor fuels to drive up to 16 hours per day, effective until December 16. Under the waiver, drivers must take a six‑hour break if they have a sleeper berth or an eight‑hour break if they do not.
The waiver replaces the standard HOS limit of 11 hours of driving within a 14‑hour window, which includes a mandatory 30‑minute break after eight hours of driving. To use the waiver, carriers must not have an out‑of‑service order, drivers must hold a valid CDL, and those with a conditional safety rating are ineligible; a physical copy of the waiver must be aboard the truck. FMCSA noted that only two other waivers remain active, one in Nebraska and one in Oregon, both tied to wildfire recovery efforts. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said the waiver helps guard against fuel shortages, lower pump costs, and ease strain on agricultural producers. The waiver took effect immediately upon announcement.
“Short-term supply chain disruptions can delay gasoline and diesel shipments, which in turn can impact freight delivery shipments,” Duffy said in the statement. “By giving truckers transporting these critical supplies the ability to drive additional hours if they are not fatigued, the agency is helping protect against shortages, lower costs for families at the pump, and reduce strain on America’s agricultural producers,” Sean Duffy, Secretary of Transportation said.
Prior to this action, FMCSA had issued mostly regional HOS waivers, with the most recent nationwide waiver lasting over two years during the COVID‑19 pandemic. The agency typically grants such waivers only for limited geographic areas, such as those tied to wildfire recovery in Nebraska and Oregon.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/trucks-hauling-fuel-get-hos-waiver-for-3-months)

item.title: TJX CEO says warehouse model helps cope with El Niño
item.description:
On Aug. 19, TJX CEO Ernie Herrman said the company’s warehouse distribution model equips it to handle El Niño-related weather swings. He explained that by keeping liquidity and shipping in warehouses, TJX can delay store shipments when unusual weather is forecast for a region.
In the hold and flow model, goods remain at distribution centers and are released to stores based on sell-through data, weather forecasts and other factors. Under the flow-through or cross-dock approach, items typically leave the DC within a day or two of arrival from suppliers. Some retailers combine both strategies, using hold and flow for seasonal, high-variety items and flow-through for low‑complexity, predictable goods. TJX’s planning organization, according to Herrman, is skilled at reacting to sudden weather shifts or natural disasters.
“[T]his is a benefit of our model where we stage goods in our warehouses versus goods at most brick-and-mortar retailers come into the warehouse and have to go out,” Ernie Herrman, CEO of TJX Companies said.
“A portion of the inventory, based on predetermined data, stops and sits in the [distribution center] and sits on the racks. And so you don’t send everything right in that moment to the stores,” Dheera Anand, partner at Bain and Co said.
Off-price retailers and classic retailers often use different inventory approaches, though no single model fits every business, according to Bain partner Dheera Anand. Anand said the hold and flow strategy described by TJX’s CEO lets retailers keep goods in distribution centers and release them based on real‑time data.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/tjx-ceo-distribution-model-will-help-weather-el-nino/830665)

item.title: Link Logistics buys four last‑mile sites adding 697,276 sq ft in DFW and Atlanta
item.description:
Link Logistics announced the acquisition of four terminals in the Dallas‑Fort Worth and Atlanta metro areas, adding 697,276 square feet of space. After the deal, Link Logistics operates over 34 million square feet in the Dallas‑Fort Worth market and more than 38 million square feet in the Atlanta area.
The acquired portfolio includes two facilities in Irving and Grand Prairie, Texas, totaling nearly 400,000 square feet, a 249,000‑square‑foot site in Suwanee, Georgia, and a smaller parcel in Farmers Branch, Texas. Link Logistics said the purchase aligns with its strategy to target infill locations supported by long‑term demand drivers. The company’s overall footprint now spans about 3,000 properties covering roughly 500 million square feet across North America.
“Our acquisition strategy is focused on expanding Link Logistics’ portfolio in infill-focused locations that are supported by strong long-term demand drivers,” Andrew Goodman, senior managing director of investments at Link Logistics said.
“Dallas-Fort Worth and Atlanta continue to see strong logistics demand as population growth and business investment support durable industrial fundamentals,” Laura Hyde, managing director of Investments at Link Logistics said.
Link Logistics already had a large presence in the Dallas‑Fort Worth and Atlanta markets before the acquisition. The Gateway Infill Growth Portfolio was sold by Oxford Properties Group. JLL represented Oxford in the transaction.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/link-logistics-buys-4-last-mile-facilities-in-dallas-fort-worth-atlanta)

item.title: Adobe Firefly data shows low‑rise silhouettes up 365% as Y2K styles surge
item.description:
Adobe Firefly analyzed AI‑generated prompts before and after New York Fashion Week, finding that consumer interest in low‑rise silhouettes jumped 365 percent. Interest in micro shorts rose even more sharply, increasing 750 percent over the same period.
Baby tees saw a 415 percent increase in prompts, while halter tops rose 260 percent and tube tops 235 percent. In beauty, prompts for graphic eyeliner and straight brows climbed approximately 450 percent year‑over‑year, and dark‑lip interest grew 400 percent. Plastic bag charms increased 300 percent this season, and beaded versions rose 290 percent, mirroring a seasonal lift for charm bracelets from September through December.
“Y2K fashion continues to have a strong influence, with growing interest in low-rise silhouettes (up 365 percent) and pieces like micro shorts (up 750 percent), baby tees (up 415 percent), halter tops (up 260 percent), tube tops (up 235 percent) and capris (up 160 percent),” Deborah Findling, creative AI trends expert at Adobe said.
The team at Adobe Firefly, a web application built on generative AI models that lets users create images, audio, videos and designs using text prompts, analyzed prompts before and after New York Fashion Week to reveal consumer trends. The software company also looked at trends from creators on Firefly’s Virtual Try On app.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/adobe-firefly-reveals-consumer-fashion-trends-y2k-low-rise-1239244298)
